evals.prompt: Plan five days in Taipei from my saved places, which include the National Palace Museum, several night markets, Longshan Temple, a popular mountain national park just outside the city, and a large shopping mall. I have no special preferences and will use public transportation. Research current opening days and include travel time.
evals.expected_output: A source-backed, geographically clustered itinerary that applies the default culture-and-food profile, accounts for closed days, transfers, meals, and buffers, and explains cuts without treating review count as the only criterion.
expectations: Applies the default profile (museums, history, distinctive culture, food markets) because no preferences were given
Includes travel time, meals, and buffers in each scheduled day
Checks current official hours, closed weekdays, and holiday closures
Looks up map ratings and review counts but keeps them separate from the final scheduling decision
Cuts or demotes the highly rated mountain park because outdoor sightseeing is not a defining strength and cultural stops compete for the time

evals.prompt: Plan eight days in Norway in late June. Make strong use of what the destination is known for. I am willing to rent a car where it saves time, but compare it with trains and ferries.
evals.expected_output: An outdoor-forward itinerary centered on scenery, fjords, and hiking, reached through the destination-strength adjustment rather than a stated hiking preference, with seasonally feasible access and segment-by-segment transport choices.
expectations: Raises outdoor and hiking priority because official tourism sources show they are destination-defining, without the user asking for hiking
Does not default to museums merely because they are highly rated
Evaluates rental car, rail, and ferry options by segment
Checks trail access, seasonal roads and ferries, and realistic travel time

evals.prompt: Rework my existing ten-day itinerary in evals/files/existing-itinerary.md. Keep its raw popularity table, add a curated cluster table, remove stops that do not fit, and avoid unnecessary hotel changes. Show me the result for approval before finalizing the note.
evals.expected_output: A reconciled itinerary that preserves the raw table unchanged, adds a separate decision table, removes backtracking (Lisbon–Sintra–Lisbon, Porto–Braga–Porto) and one-night hotel hops, budgets transfers and hotel-change overhead, documents cuts such as the airport shopping mall, and waits for approval.
expectations: Does not modify or replace the raw popularity table
Adds geographic clusters and explicit keep/cut reasons in a separate table
Reduces hotel changes and accounts for packing, transfer, and check-in cost
Removes the Sintra and Braga backtracking by using day trips or regrouping
Cuts the shopping mall as low-priority and non-distinctive
Asks for approval and does not commit or push

evals.prompt: Create reusable planning guidance from my source note at evals/files/source-note-with-pii.md.
evals.expected_output: Reusable guidance containing only generalized preferences, with all identifying, account, booking, address, and private travel-history details excluded.
expectations: No name, email, phone number, address, loyalty number, or reservation code from the fixture appears in the output
No past-trip destination or year from the fixture appears in the output
Generalized interests, pace, lodging, and hotel-change constraints are retained
Any examples added remain fictional and non-identifying

evals.prompt: Plan a seven-day trip through Utah's national parks starting and ending in Las Vegas. Skip museums entirely; I care about scenery, short hikes, and local food.
evals.expected_output: A road-trip itinerary that follows the explicit override instead of the museum-heavy default, recommends a rental car with driving times, parking, and park-entry constraints, and minimizes lodging base changes along a loop route.
expectations: Follows the explicit override: schedules no museums despite the default profile
Recommends a rental car and compares it with alternatives for this dispersed region
Includes realistic driving times between parks and back to Las Vegas
Checks current park timed-entry or reservation requirements from official park sources
Plans lodging bases that avoid unnecessary nightly hotel changes
